Section 2 - Purpose
(1)
The University aims to be an employer of choice for current and prospective staff. The University is committed to attracting and retaining high performing academic and professional staff and recognising and rewarding outstanding performance.
(2)
This Policy provides guidance to University managers to ensure the consistent application of remuneration and reward outcomes that are:
market competitive
fair and equitable
structured to ensure gender pay equality
legally compliant; and
within the ‘capacity to pay’ of the University

Section 3 - Scope
(3)
This Policy is applicable to all staff members who are directly engaged in employment through either:
the
La Trobe University Enterprise Agreement 2023
, approved by the Fair Work Commission (the ‘
Enterprise Agreement
’); or
Executive Senior Management Contracts.

Section 4 - Key Decisions
Key Decisions
Role
Approve the University’s remuneration strategy
Vice-Chancellor

Section 5 - Policy Statement
(4)
Remuneration is the term used to describe a staff members’ employment in the form of salary and/or benefits and/or incentives.

Section 6 - Procedures
(6)
Please refer to:
Remuneration and Benefits Procedure - Academic Leadership Allowances
Remuneration and Benefits Procedure - Executive and Senior Management Classification
Remuneration and Benefits Procedure - Salary Loadings
Remuneration and Benefits Procedure - Senior Staff Annual Remuneration Review

Section 7 - Definitions
(7)
For the purpose of this Policy:
Classification refers to:
the placement of positions for both academic, professional and administrative staff within La Trobe University classification structures as defined by the relevant framework in the
Enterprise Agreement
; and
The placement of senior level positions within the Executive and Senior management Classification (ESMC) structure as defined by Mercer classification model deployed at the University.
Remuneration is the term used to describe the reward for employment in the form of salary and/or benefits and/or incentives.
Superannuation is the arrangement the staff member makes to have funds available for them in retirement. Superannuation in Australia is governed by federal legislation which includes the setting of minimum contribution levels. Superannuation payment contributions are made on Ordinary Time Earnings into the staff member’s super fund by the University and, where elected by the staff member, topped up by the staff member’s own payment contribution.
The University: is La Trobe University.

Section 8 - Authority and Associated Information
(8)
This Policy is made under the
La Trobe University Act 2009
.
